title: Testing painted vs unpainted water in my AI-assisted RPG
author: TarinRook
selftext:
To paint or not to paint that is the question.   
First view is painted, second is my usual default.   
What do you guys think?   
  
I'm thinking of painting the entire world.   
Well it was always the plan and it already kind of is painted but I'm really trying to break away from that default unreal look. To get to this point I've tried just about every ai tool you can think of. One that's been working wonders is asset furnace, it's free and modifiable and saves you from having to pay for trippo. I even got it working on my AMD card.   
  
Another thing that's huge for development for me has been around since my very first week 2 months ago. And that is the Dev Pin. Basically the dev pin lets me play a build of my game, and while I'm playing it I can drop pins that save coordinates, take a screenshot, and then I can speak or type what I want to fix/change/add. My llm can then search these pins and implement what I wanted from the dev pins I dropped. And I have dropped thousands of them.   
  
I have a game dev lab in my browser that collects all the gates and blockers and keeps track of our development progress with roadmaps and lane availability and office for each llm that has worked on the project, I even added a jukebox for the games music that was mostly created in suno.   
Voice lines are 11labs v4, originally I was dubbing everything myself and had built a sound booth in browser with director and options to 11 labs, but v4 made it so I no longer had to dub every line myself and honestly, v4 is a much better actor than I am.   
  
But I haven't been able to remove the taint of unreal lighting and other things that scream unreal.   
And this brings us to operation paint the taint. The world was always supposed to be painterly, but only in a few spots have I said to myself "This looks like a painting".



And for the painted water iteration I took a screenshot and generated a target image:

![img](6r90my2sf92i1 "Sceencap vs Target")

Sent this prompt to GPT lets see if you can generate the image im looking for from this prompt, focusing on the water. " I like it, we can even make it more apparent where the water is flowing to i think as well. like make sure the strokes follow the actual path the water would have to take example here: you can see the paint in the waterfall pond is all statically going the same direction; perhaps we could form our strokes so they look like they are all flowing toward our rive point.  
  
It generated a target image. Then I sent that target image back to claude with this prompt: "**The painted water looks good, but the flow direction needs to read better. In the waterfall pond, the strokes currently feel too static and too uniform. Please reshape the brushwork so it follows the actual water motion: turbulent circular flow under the waterfall, then a clear directional pull toward the river outflow. Also line up the seams between water regions so the painterly surface feels continuous. Preserve the painted style, but make the brush strokes communicate the real flow of the water."**

And now claude his running another diff study and is going to take his best effort. Credits are running thin this week and reset is on Friday. Hopefully we can finish the water by tomorrow and it looks more like that target image!
